title: Majestic Trick
reviewNotes: Three branches, 32 exact positions from complete seven-piece board. a6 and Ne3+ lure ...Bxe3 before a forcing queen-skewer route through Qg2/Qg5/Qf5/Qd7 wins Qd1. Immediate axb6 draws. Correction: rushed a7 ...dxc2 a8=Q ...c1=Q is also drawn at every encoded step, not a Black win as claimed in the source. Both correction and exact evidence retained.
transcript: Fools will resign. Wise players might make a draw, but only a true genius would be able to win from this position. But playing with white is the king of skewers and he has found an incredible idea that will allow him to win this position. The first move is A6 trying to promote on A8. Black has no way to prevent the promotion with the bishop. So instead, it gives this check to avoid the knight seeing the bishop and then it starts pushing this pawn. Now pushing would be a massive mistake. After we lose this knight, yes, we are both going to get a queen, but white is now down a pawn and a bishop. What's the big deal? Where is the win? White is just down a bishop and a pawn, but you see this bishop has been lured to the worst possible square. And now white can play queen to F5 and forces the king to the D file. If only the king could go to E3, but it can't. And so, after it moves, we're going to skewer [music] the king again and pick up the queen, winning the game.
